problem: Whether the variance-scaled normalized Turán deficit V·δ_D at the first-descent index D of a Poisson–binomial pmf is bounded below by a universal constant once V ≥ 1.
debate: Quantitative log-concavity (Newton/Turán-inequality deficits) for Poisson–binomial pmfs, with the opening naming only Newton's inequalities and a survey [9] and deferring the prior δ_k bounds to a later section instead of citing them here.
gap: Known lower bounds on δ_k scale with n or with the success probabilities, so they degenerate when summands with p_i near 0 or 1 pile up at fixed variance.
contribution: A proof that V·δ_D ≥ 1/4 whenever V ≥ 1 (partly computer-assisted, via Hillion–Johnson and Bobkov–Marsiglietti–Melbourne bounds), the corollary f_{D+r}/f_D ≤ exp(−r/(4V)), and a binomial family showing the best constant is at most 1/3.
note: The theorem is crisp and the sharpness example earns it a look, but page one never names the prior δ_k bounds you claim to beat and gives no reason anyone needs V·δ_D beyond its own interest, so fix that or the first referee will ask 'so what?'
